rows.interest: designing the vehicles of the future
rows.attribution: The current bachelor public page describes smarter, cleaner and safer car systems, but explicitly says students are not specifically trained to develop a car; interpret this interest as automotive-system innovation.
The current bachelor public page explicitly connects the programme to hybrid and electric cars; the core includes propulsion and power electronics.
The current bachelor public page explicitly identifies self-driving cars as a motivating development; optional perception/autonomous-vehicle courses are not universal core.
The current bachelor public page describes cars as connected intelligent high-tech systems; no separate Smart Mobility bachelor track is claimed.
The current bachelor public page explicitly emphasises electronics and software; computer architecture, programming, electronic circuits and sensing/computing/actuating are required.

rows.interest: reducing the environmental impact of transport
rows.attribution: The current bachelor public page identifies cleaner cars and reducing CO2 emissions as motivations; this does not make every environmental topic compulsory.
Required5EC Road Vehicle Dynamics and the formal additional mechanics/static/dynamic learning outcome directly support this interest.
Required5EC Propulsion Systems and the formal energy-conversion outcome directly support this direction; detailed engine coverage is not inferred solely from the title.
The current bachelor public page names safer cars. Safety/reliability is a programme application, not a separately verified compulsory safety-engineering module.
The current bachelor public page describes connections to other systems, and Vehicle Networking is required; general connectivity rather than a specific protocol is established.

Interpretive application within the independently verified electric/hybrid mobility and energy-conversion direction. The inspected curriculum does not establish a separately compulsory battery-systems module or battery specialization.
The current bachelor public page names smart traffic measuring systems and reducing traffic jams. Cooperative-driving detail is a related application, not a verified named bachelor route.
The formal Automotive outcomes add mechanics and mechanical-energy conversion to the Electrical Engineering core; electromechanics, circuits and vehicle dynamics make the integration substantive.
Sensing, Computing and Actuating and Control Systems are required; acquisition of physical quantities and control/actuation are explicit formal learning outcomes.

Interpretive energy-efficiency direction grounded in cleaner/electric/hybrid vehicle motivations and compulsory energy-conversion/power-electronics/propulsion study; no particular vehicle design brief is promised.

rows.interest: the integration of complex vehicle systems
rows.attribution: The current bachelor public page explicitly teaches understanding the car as a system; formal outcomes address artefact design and management of complexity.
Interpretive transport application of the current cleaner-car/mobility motivation. No compulsory separate personal-versus-commercial transport pathway is established.
